principles.P-a: A verdict bullet that is a property (uniqueness, necessity, best-practice defaults, orderly reconnection) may be shown violated by observation plus third-party references, even in a conceptual case (Rule R2); PASS stays unreachable.
principles.P-b: A verdict bullet that refers to an IXIT field (e.g. 'Provisioning Mechanism', 'Generation Mechanism', 'documented as such') is a comparison with the IXIT (Rule R1) and contributes no reachable verdict.
principles.P-c: A PASS over a universal quantifier ('each/every/all components') must not be reached by assuming the observed sample is complete; that assumes the conclusion. A FAIL from one counterexample is allowed.
principles.P-d: Verdicts that rest on the results of the tester's own attacks are unreachable; a conceptual case whose only passive route duplicates its functional counterpart is not counted again.
principles.P-e: Under Model N the purpose or consent basis of processing cannot be taken from the manufacturer's documents; verdicts that need it are unreachable under N (they may be reachable under ND).

decisions.note: Uniqueness is a property; a cleartext credential matching a published universal-default list shows violation.
Impracticability is a property; unthrottled third-party guessing captured in traffic shows violation (opportunistic).
Public CVE left unfixed in the observed firmware version indicates untimely action; the confirmation bullet keeps PASS unreachable.
Indications of misuse come from the tester's attacks; plaintext update downloads are a cue only.
PASS needs every component covered; observing one update path cannot show that.
Observing automatic installs does not show the user-facing configurability the verdict requires.
Periodic checks for one mechanism cannot show every component is covered.
Same reasoning as 5.2-2-1 for deployment of security updates.
Both bullets are framed on IXIT fields ('documented as such', 'Provisioning Mechanism').
Bullets refer to 'Description' and 'Generation Mechanism' IXIT fields.
The passive route (unauthenticated access observed) is the functional case 5.5-4-2, already fail_only.
As 5.5-4-1; covered by 5.5-5-2.
Necessity of disclosed information can be judged against protocol specifications; versions not required by the protocol show violation.
Orderly, standard-conformant reconnection is a property; tight retry loops violating protocol RFCs show violation.
After an opportunistic user reset, user identifiers still sent show unsuccessful erasure.
Insecure defaults visible out of the box (e.g. UPnP mappings, plaintext services) violate best-practice defaults.
Opportunistic malformed inbound input followed by a crash or error leak indicates missing validation.
Which processing is consent-based is known only from the manufacturer; reachable under ND only.
Necessity needs the intended purpose; inferring it from the device category is not a third-party reference.
